sections.heading: Duration of symptoms and conservative therapy (criteria C1 and C2)
sections.text: Symptoms must have lasted at least 6 weeks. Conservative therapy means at least 6 weeks of one or more of: supervised physical therapy or a structured home exercise program, NSAIDs or other analgesics unless contraindicated, activity modification, or chiropractic care. The record should state what was tried, for how long, and the response. A plan to start physical therapy does not count as a completed trial.

sections.heading: Red-flag findings (criterion RF1)
sections.text: Red flags justify imaging without a trial of conservative therapy. They include saddle anesthesia, new urinary retention or overflow incontinence, new fecal incontinence, bilateral or progressive leg weakness, foot drop that is worsening, a history of cancer with new back pain, unexplained weight loss, fever with back pain or intravenous drug use, and significant trauma or osteoporosis with suspected fracture. Stable, long-standing numbness alone is not a red flag.

sections.heading: Scope
sections.text: This policy applies to requests for MRI of the lumbar spine without contrast for adult members. Most acute low back pain improves within 4 to 6 weeks with conservative care, and early imaging without red flags does not improve outcomes. Imaging is therefore indicated either immediately when red flags are present, or after a documented failed trial of conservative therapy when the result will guide a procedure.
